speaker_role: current university administrator (Meg Lysy, Senior Director for Alumni Relations, Dartmouth College; previously ran Georgetown's required alumni interview program)
commercial_incentive: None evident from the guest; podcast host's own affiliation (CMAC) is unclear from transcript
key_insights: Dartmouth's alumni interview program involves 6,000-8,000 volunteer alumni interviewers annually conducting roughly 18,000-20,000 interviews out of an applicant pool that grew from about 20,000 (2015) to over 30,000 now, meaning not every applicant gets matched with an interviewer, purely due to regional volunteer availability
Interviewers must re-commit annually and agree to a code of conduct, protection-of-minors policy, and confidentiality, reflecting significant institutional oversight given volunteers meet with minors

Dartmouth's oldest-in-the-country Book Award program has local alumni give a book to a high-achieving junior at local high schools as an early recruitment/relationship-building touchpoint (600 awarded nationally, with a single Boston-area coordinator alone covering awards across roughly 125 different high schools)

Some peer institutions have eliminated alumni interviewing programs, likely due to oversight burden, risk of inconsistent volunteer quality, and the extra 'barrier to applying' it creates for a school trying to maximize application volume - while Dartmouth leans into it because admitted-student survey data shows applicants value getting a first personal touchpoint with the school

Every admitted Dartmouth student typically has some alumni connection already established by the time of yield, since interviews happen pre-decision, which the school treats as a meaningful factor in convincing admits to enroll
specific_numbers_or_facts: Dartmouth applicant pool grew from ~20,000 in 2015 to 30,000+ currently (per speaker)
600 Dartmouth Book Awards given nationally each year; one Boston-area chair alone coordinates awards across ~125 high schools
notable_or_distinctive: Direct account from the administrator who actually runs a major university's alumni interviewing operation, including candid discussion of why peer schools have dropped similar programs (oversight burden, risk, and reduced application funnel) while Dartmouth deliberately keeps it as a differentiator.
reliability_notes: Reflects Dartmouth's specific program and philosophy, which will not generalize to schools without similarly resourced/robust alumni networks; figures are stated by the guest without independent verification but she speaks with direct institutional authority on her own program.
